indicator_definition: The income quintile share ratio (S80/S20) is the ratio of total equivalised disposable income received by the top 20% of the population to that received by the bottom 20%. A higher value indicates greater income inequality. Data are drawn from the EU Survey on Income and Living Conditions (EU-SILC).
rationale: Income inequality undermines social cohesion and limits life opportunities for those at the lower end of the income distribution. Reducing inequality is a prerequisite for sustainable and inclusive growth. Progress means a decreasing S80/S20 ratio over time.
methodology_characteristics: Data are collected through EU-SILC. Equivalised disposable income is the total household income after tax and other deductions, divided by the equivalised household size. The survey is conducted annually in all participating countries.
